correctness.rationale: From \(x_1=Ax_0/u\), \(x_2\) is proportional to \(((a^2+\beta u)c,(b^2+\beta u)s)\); exact Rayleigh subtraction has strictly positive denominator and numerator sign \(a^2b^2-(\beta u)^2\). Distinct positive eigenvalues ensure no zero denominator. Haar-circle first coordinate squared has \(\operatorname{Beta}(1/2,1/2)\) law, giving the exact arccos tail and inverse risk cap; the two square-root cusp constants follow by Taylor expansion. Standard-library verifier passed 8,000 exact fraction algebra tests, 40,000 direct update tests, 36 circular probability grids, and endpoint asymptotics. Simulation is secondary to proof.

value.rationale: The one-step Rayleigh loss is a natural and operationally meaningful risk for parameterizing the newly proposed two-sweep eigenvalue solver. Exact zero/mixed/one phases, a sharp universal safety threshold, and the full risk-constrained coefficient inversion give a complete two-spectral-mode benchmark. It is not a normalization caveat, arbitrary numerical slice, or an unmotivated tiny improvement: it separates safely accelerated updates from loss of a central computed quantity under random starts. No claims are made for a full GPR-based trajectory.
